content.value_statement: Go collection code can become repetitive and hard to review. This skill shows when to use samber/lo helpers in modern Go projects.
actual_capabilities: Shows the go get command for github.com/samber/lo v1.
Lists imports for lo, parallel, mutable, and iterator packages.
Demonstrates Filter, Map, Find, Uniq, GroupBy, and Must usage.
Points users to the public lo function list for newer helpers.
Warns users to compare online function lists with local dependency versions.
limitations: It does not replace the official samber/lo API documentation.
It does not run Go tests or verify module compatibility.
It covers common examples, not the full samber/lo package surface.
It includes a curl documentation lookup that requires network access.

use_cases.title: Modernize collection helpers
use_cases.description: Convert simple filtering, mapping, grouping, and lookup logic into clear samber/lo helper usage.

use_cases.title: Review helper adoption
use_cases.description: Check whether lo helpers improve readability or whether explicit loops remain clearer.

use_cases.title: Learn common patterns
use_cases.description: Understand the main lo imports and function families before adding the library to a project.

prompt_templates.title: Identify useful helpers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go task and suggest which samber/lo helpers could make it clearer. Explain when a plain loop is better.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor collection logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Help refactor this Go collection logic with samber/lo. Keep behavior unchanged and explain each helper choice.

prompt_templates.title: Audit lo usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this samber/lo usage for readability, version compatibility, panic risk, and unnecessary helper chains.

prompt_templates.title: Plan library adoption
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan for adopting samber/lo across a Go service. Include version checks, testing scope, and review rules.

output_examples.input: A Go service has repeated loops for filtering and mapping user records.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend Filter and Map where readability improves, while keeping explicit loops for stateful logic.

output_examples.input: A reviewer sees Must used in request handling code.
output_examples.output: The skill would flag panic risk and recommend normal error handling outside initialization paths.

output_examples.input: A team wants the newest lo helper list.
output_examples.output: The skill would direct them to the public function list and remind them to verify their installed module version.

best_practices: Confirm the installed samber/lo version before using newer helpers.
Use Must only for initialization or truly unrecoverable setup.
Prefer explicit loops when helper chains hide important control flow.
anti_patterns: Replacing every loop with a helper call by default.
Using the latest online function list without checking local dependencies.
Using parallel or mutable helpers without reviewing race and mutation behavior.

faq.question: What Go version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Go 1.18 and newer projects that can use generics.

faq.question: Does it install samber/lo automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents the install command, but the user controls dependency changes.

faq.question: Can it replace official documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a quick guide and should be checked against the official API.

faq.question: Does it cover every lo helper?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on common helpers and points to the public function list.

faq.question: Is Must safe in all code paths?
faq.answer: No. Must can panic, so it is best for initialization and setup failures.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
